To: d.kerrigan@northmail.example
Replying to: m01
Cc: none
Subject: Re: Blister packs for my mother - new patient

Dear Mr. Kerrigan,

Thank you for contacting Erindale Park Pharmacy. I'm sorry to hear about your mother's fall, and I'm glad she is well enough to go home on Thursday. We would be happy to look after her, and I'll do my best to have everything ready for her. My answers to your questions are below.

1. Blister packs and cost
Yes, we prepare weekly blister packs. Each pack covers seven days, with up to four dosing times a day. There is no charge for the packaging. Your mother would only pay the regular dispensing fees, and because she is 81, the Ontario Drug Benefit program will cover most of her medication costs.

2. Delivery or pickup
We deliver free of charge within 8 km, and her building on Mississauga Valley Blvd is well within that. Our regular deliveries are on Tuesdays and Fridays between 2 and 6 pm. For her first packs this week, you can pick them up at the store, or we can make a one-time delivery to her on Saturday before 1 pm. Please let me know which you prefer.

3. Moving her prescriptions
You don't need to do anything with her old pharmacy. We will call them and arrange the transfer. We only need the pharmacy's name and address and her OHIP number. Because the OHIP number is personal information, you're welcome to give it to us by phone instead of email.

4. Speaking with you about her medications
I'm glad to work with you on this, and I understand it is easier for your mother if you handle the details. Before we can discuss her medications with you, we need her permission. We record it on a short form called the Family Communication Consent, which she signs. This is our standard practice for every patient, and it protects her privacy. She can sign it when the first packs are picked up, or our driver can bring it to her on Saturday. As soon as it is signed, I can go through her medication list with you in as much detail as you like.

I would also like to offer your mother a MedsCheck during her first week home. This is a free review of about 20 minutes, done by a pharmacist after a hospital stay. We go through all her medications, old and new, to make sure everything is clear and nothing overlaps. I can come to her condo on Monday or Tuesday after 6 pm, so you could be there too after work. Let me know which evening suits you.

Timing and two requests
We need about 48 hours to prepare the first packs once we have all of her prescriptions, meaning both the discharge prescriptions and the transfers. To keep the timing as short as possible:

- Please ask the hospital to fax her discharge prescriptions to us early on Thursday morning. If we receive them then, her first packs should be ready on Saturday.
- Because the packs won't be ready on Thursday, please confirm with the discharge team that she will go home with an interim supply of her medications. Please also make sure someone can help her with each dose from Thursday until the packs arrive on Saturday. With several new medications and her recent confusion with pills, I don't want her managing on her own during those two days.

If you have any questions or would like to talk before Thursday, you can reach me directly at 905-555-0148, ext. 2. I'm in the store Monday to Friday, 9 am to 6 pm.

Thank you for choosing us. We look forward to taking care of your mother.

Kind regards,

Rania Haddad
Pharmacist
Erindale Park Pharmacy
905-555-0148 ext. 2
